investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T08:26–08:33Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for ~142–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent identity or VM was provisioned, and the eval produced zero evidence, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion condition, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which submits a pod that cannot be scheduled, so the probe never reaches the point of writing any evidence, causing a total contract gap against the four required fields declared in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and making the cluster effectively a 2-node pool for this workload.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod creation attempt was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the remote-agent-state expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable slots available and preemption unable to free any (no lower-priority victims found), every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent with type "remote") depends on a successfully scheduled pod before it can collect any evidence; the scheduling failure causes the probe to time out and report the scheduler error message verbatim, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json, line 264) fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T08:26–08:33Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for ~142–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent identity or VM was provisioned, and the eval produced zero evidence, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion condition, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which submits a pod that cannot be scheduled, so the probe never reaches the point of writing any evidence, causing a total contract gap against the four required fields declared in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 08:28 and 08:33 UTC on 2026-07-03 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes had insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving every new remote-agent pod permanently unschedulable. Because the pod never started, the eval runner received no evidence output, causing all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be missing and the expected-output assertion on message containing "hello from aura" to go unevaluated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on its 2 VM-capable nodes. Every pod submitted by the eval runner for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime was rejected by the scheduler with "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption was not possible. The pods remained unschedulable for 142–148 seconds until the eval timeout fired, producing empty evidence and a contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 VM-capable nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval pods. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same scheduler message within a 5-minute window.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so even if VM slots were available on other nodes the pods could not be placed there. This is a structural constraint, not a transient one.

Tertiary — VM slot leak or slow release: a previous eval run or user workload may have allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that were not released before this eval run began, temporarily exhausting capacity. This would be transient and self-resolving.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: the cluster may have too few kata-capable nodes or too few VM slots per node to absorb simultaneous eval probes across remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime without contention.
